newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-JONES JOINS HUNT WITH SECOND ROUND 65.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES JOINS HUNT WITH SECOND ROUND 65.

text.p: Former U.S. Open champion Steve Jones shot a second round six-under-par 65 to force himself into contention in the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Thursday.

The American's score, sparked by a birdie three at the third, propelled him into a share of the lead at eight-under with overnight pacesetters, Joakim Haeggman of Sweden and Briton Paul Curry, who had not begun their rounds.
Both shot 63 on Wednesday in the final European Tour event before next week's British Open at Royal Troon.

Jones held a two-stroke lead among the early finishers on world number two Greg Norman, who compiled his second successive 68 which he said was "the worst it could have been. I missed chances, especially at the last three holes."

Jones, who scored a mammoth 11-stroke victory in the Phoenix Open this year with a 26-under-par winning total, has gone off the boil since then, missing halfway cuts at the Players' Championship, the Masters, the Heritage Classic and the Colonial events.
"It was all because of a swing flaw which I didn't realise I had," he said. "I was trying to do one thing and I should have been doing the opposite.

"Someone else's teacher told me I was taking the club inside too much on the backswing," he said. "He told me to take it back straighter. I worked on it and it quickly felt that I was swinging better."
Jones began his charge by rifling a two-iron approach to eight feet at the 505-yard third and holing the putt for an eagle.
He birdied the sixth and ninth from eight and six feet, the short 11th from 20 feet and the 14th from 12 feet before his only bogey at the 15th, where he tangled with a bunker.
He immediately clawed that stroke back with a 25-footer at the next.
Conditions were tougher, an early morning chill and breeze stiffening the course after Wednesday's perfect conditions.
Norman bogeyed the short fifth after missing the green but had five birdies in the next nine holes including one on a putt of 66 feet at the seventh.
"I think someone will reach at least 10-under today, but I'm in there with a chance," he said.

Nick Faldo may have blown his chance with a two-over 73 for 140. "I didn't play well at all and when I got close, I missed," he said. "I was fine on the practice range, then it felt wrong from the first swing.
